question: A car runs 40 minutes at a speed of 45 km/h, next 45 minutes at a speed of 60 km/h and1{ {1} over 2} hours at a speed of 50 km/h. The average speed (in km/h) of the car for the whole journey is closest to:
solution:
Given:

Speed of car in first 40 min = 45 km/h

Speed of car in next 60 min = 60 km/h

Speed of car in last 1.5 hours (90 min) = 50 km/h

Concept used:

Average speed = (Total distance covered)/(Total time taken)

Distance = Time × Speed 

Calculation:

Distance covered in the 40 minutes = 45 × 40/60 = 30 km

Distance covered in the 45 minutes = 60 × 45/60 = 45 km

Distance covered in the 1.5 hours = 50 × 1.5 = 75 km

Total distance covered = 30 + 45 + 75 = 150 km

Total time taken = 40/60 + 45/60 + 1.5

⇒ 2/3 + 3/4 + 3/2

⇒ 35/12 hours

Now, the average speed of the car for the whole journey = 150/(35/12)

⇒ 51.428 km/h ≈ 51.4 km/h

**∴ The average speed of car for the whole journey is closest to 51.4 km/h.**
